record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: A problem is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter p if instances (I, p) can be solved in time f(p)|I|^O(1) for some computable function f depending only on p. An AT-free graph is a graph with no asteroidal triple. Is the Coloring problem fixed-parameter tractable on AT-free graphs when the parameter is the number k of colors?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Is Coloring fixed-parameter tractable for AT-free graphs when parameterized by k?
A problem is called fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) if every instance (I, p) of it can be solved in time f(p)|I|O(1)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A parameterized decision problem is fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) with respect to a parameter p if every instance (I,p) can be decided in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f depending only on p.

In a graph G=(V,E), an asteroidal triple is a set of three pairwise non-adjacent vertices such that between any two of them there is a path avoiding the closed neighborhood of the third. A graph is AT-free if it contains no asteroidal triple.

The Coloring problem takes as input a graph G and a positive integer k, and asks whether there is a proper k-coloring of G, i.e., a map c:V→{1,…,k} with c(u)≠c(v) whenever uv∈E.

Question: Is the Coloring problem, restricted to AT-free input graphs and parameterized by the number k of colors, fixed-parameter tractable?
artifact.status_search_result: The parameterized complexity of Coloring on AT-free graphs (with k as parameter) is listed as an open problem in a survey on graph coloring open problems for special graph classes. Web search did not surface a subsequent resolution; related work (Kratsch–Müller on Coloring AT-free graphs) addresses other complexity aspects but not the FPT question. Status appears to remain open.
